To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in systems with MMSE multiuser receivers: the output MAI is approximately Gaussian with very high probability; and the network capacity is close to that corresponding to the optimal signatures at the cost of a small amount of transmission power.

the output MAI of an MMSE receiver in a wireless system with random spreading is approximately Gaussian and the network capacity corresponding the MMSE receiver can be made arbitrarily close to that corresponding to the optimal signatures.

the conditional distribution (given signatures and received powers) of the output interference of MMSE multiuser receivers converges to Gaussian in the large system, and the network capacity of systems with random signatures can be expressed explicitly and is arbitrarily close to that of systems with optimal signatures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of the MMSE receivers in systems with random signatures, and the results provide a theoretical basis for the design and implementation of systems with random signatures.
the performance of MMSE receivers in large wireless systems.
the performance of the MMSE receivers in systems with random spreading, where the signatures are assumed to be random and take values over complex space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
systems with MMSe receivers are robust to randomness of signatures, and that the network capacity of such systems is close to that of systems with optimal signatures.
the randomness of the signature sequences is not a problem in the sense that the performance of the MMSE receivers can be analyzed and optimized as in systems with deterministic signatures.
the randomness of the spreading sequences has a negligible effect on the system performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a system with MMSE receivers, randomness in the signature design is not only beneficial in reducing the complexity, but also in enhancing the network capacity.
systems with MMSe receivers are robust to both the randomness of the received power and the randomness of the spreading signatures.
, in large systems, MMSE receivers are capable of achieving near-optimal network capacity, even when the signatures are random.
The main takeaway from our work is that
systems with random spreading and MMSE receivers can approach the network capacity corresponding the optimal signature allocation at the cost of a slight increase in the transmission power.
the MMSE receiver, which is widely used in practice, is robust to the randomness in signatures.
, in systems with MMSE multiuser receivers, the randomness of the spreading sequences does not affect the network capacity significantly, as long as the QoS requirements are met.
